how_to_use: For each case run your scanner on tool_name, arguments and (when present) metadata, and compare scanned and findings exactly (order included) with 'expected'. Cases with source 'server' were generated from the enforcer; 'spec' cases express a rule the server does not apply (scanner bounds). Group 'known_divergence' records what the Python server answers for text where Unicode and ASCII regex semantics differ; skip it for conformance.

cases.note: Python \b is Unicode: 'é' is a word character, so no boundary. ASCII engines count 1.
Python \w includes CJK letters, so no boundary before the address. ASCII engines count 1.
Python \d matches Unicode digits. ASCII engines count 0.
Python \s matches U+00A0; RE2 does not. Counts differ by engine.
root is depth 0; the leaf is at depth 16, the last visited depth
leaf at depth 17 is not visited: dlp and recipient are left out of scanned, with their findings. The server's own scan goes to depth 32 and would count both.
